tools.name: screen_mark
tools.description:
Screens one brand name against trademark registers. No account needed.

    Returns the registered and pending marks closest to the name (up to 25), each with a
    similarity tier, and the registers those marks are filed in. EU marks come from
    EUIPO's search; the other registers are read from A

tools.name: check_names
tools.description:
Screens a shortlist of up to 15 candidate names in one call: the trademarks on
    file near each name, the companies registered under it, and whether its domains are
    registered. Ranks them fewest conflicts first: by how close the nearest mark is, then
    by companies registered under the name

    Computed from their whole register book: how much of it they let lapse, whether
    their marks cluster where they trade or spray across unrelated classes, and the

tools.description:

    Twenty registers, each with the provision the window comes from. The trap this
    answers: most offices run opposition BEFORE registration, from publication of the

tools.name: filing_landscape
tools.description:
Filing activity in a Nice class — volume by month and the busiest filers. Signed-in.

    Answers "how crowded is my space" and "who keeps filing near me". Pass a Nice
    class (9, 42, 36…), optionally an office code ('EM', 'US', 'GB', 'CH'), and a
    window in months.

tools.name: my_conflicts
tools.description: Everything currently near the names this user watches.

tools.name: my_deadlines
my_watches
tools.description: The names this user is watching.

tools.name: company_file
tools.description:
A holder's WHOLE book across every office. Founder and up.

    Corporate identity from PermID (organisation, HQ, PermID) comes with
    `company.attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

tools.name: follow_filer
tools.description:
Follow an adversary — every filing they make, anywhere. Studio and up.

    Different from watching a name: this catches what they do NEXT, which is usually
    a different name in a class the user doesn't hold.

tools.name: watch_mark
tools.description:
Start watching a brand name: new filings near it show up as conflicts.

    Optionally takes Nice classes as a comma-separated list ('9,42'); blank watches
    every class.

tools.name: dismiss_conflict
tools.description:
Clear one hit as not-a-threat. Reversible — it moves to the Cleared list.

    Takes `jurisdiction` and `app_no` exactly as they appear on a conflict in the
    user's conflict list. A cleared hit, such as an unrelated business or the user's
    own filing, stops being surfaced.

tools.name: filer_activity
tools.description: What the filers this user follows have filed lately. Studio and up.

tools.name: run_investigation
tools.description:
Research a trademark holder on the open web and return a cited dossier: who they
    really are (an operating company, a shell, a known squatter), their notable
    trademark activity or disputes, and any red flags. Signed-in.

    Spends one credit — included credits first, then purchased ones. A f

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description:
How many credits this user can spend and what each paid tool costs, in credits.
    Free to call.

    `remaining` is what can be spent now: `monthly_left` (included with their plan,
    resets each month) plus `topup_balance` (bought, never expires). `prices` is
    credits per call, by tool.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_names" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
